content:
Heathrow is the UK's busiest airport — and for passengers travelling from Henfield and West Sussex, it is also one of the most common departure points for long-haul flights to the Americas, Asia, the Middle East, and beyond.

Getting there smoothly is not complicated, but it does require a bit of planning. The distance, the terminal complexity, and the sheer scale of the airport mean that a well-organised transfer makes a genuine difference to how your journey begins.

This guide covers everything you need to know about travelling from Henfield to Heathrow — including journey times, terminal information, meet and greet options, and why a pre-booked private transfer is almost always the right choice.

How Far Is Henfield from Heathrow Airport?

Heathrow sits on the western edge of Greater London, approximately 55 miles from Henfield. The most common route takes you north on the A281 through Horsham, then onto the M23 and M25 before joining the M4 or the Heathrow spur road.

Under normal conditions, the journey takes around 70 to 90 minutes. However, Heathrow is notorious for variable traffic conditions, particularly:

  • The M25 between junctions 7 and 15 — one of the busiest stretches of motorway in Europe, prone to delays at almost any time of day
  • The M4 corridor — heavy during morning and evening rush hours
  • Airport approach roads — can queue significantly during peak departure periods
For most Heathrow flights, we recommend allowing at least 2.5 to 3 hours from your front door to clearing security. For long-haul flights where check-in opens 3 hours before departure, plan accordingly.

Heathrow's Five Terminals — Which One Do You Need?

Heathrow has five passenger terminals, and knowing which one you need before you travel is essential. Arriving at the wrong terminal adds time and stress to the start of your journey.

Here is a quick guide to which airlines use which terminal:

  • Terminal 2 (The Queen's Terminal) — Star Alliance carriers including United, Lufthansa, Air Canada, Singapore Airlines, and others
  • Terminal 3 — oneworld and SkyTeam carriers including American Airlines, Cathay Pacific, Delta, Emirates, and Virgin Atlantic
  • Terminal 4 — KLM, Malaysia Airlines, and some other carriers
  • Terminal 5 — British Airways exclusively (the largest terminal at Heathrow)
Always check your booking confirmation or the Heathrow website to confirm your terminal before travel. Your Western Cars driver will also confirm this when you book.

Tips for Travelling from Henfield to Heathrow

Book early, especially for early morning departures. Heathrow has a significant number of flights departing between 6am and 9am. Demand for transfers during these hours is high. Booking in advance guarantees your driver is allocated to your journey.

Allow extra time for the M25. Even at 5am, the M25 around Heathrow can be unpredictable. We build contingency into our journey times, but it is always better to arrive at the airport with time to spare than to be rushing through check-in.

Confirm your terminal when you book. This is the single most common source of confusion for Heathrow passengers. Double-check your booking confirmation and pass the terminal number to us when you book — it ensures your driver drops you at exactly the right place.

Consider the Heathrow Express for the return journey. If you are arriving back into Heathrow and your onward journey involves central London, the Heathrow Express to Paddington is fast and reliable. For passengers heading back to Henfield and West Sussex, however, a private transfer remains the most convenient option — particularly late at night or with heavy luggage.
